steps.line: Hindu tradition thinks about time in huge circles. Worlds are made, they last for ages, they dissolve, and then they begin again.

steps.q: Hindu texts measure one day of Brahma, the creator. Roughly how long is it?
steps.why: One kalpa, a day of Brahma, is 4.32 billion human years, and his night is as long again. That’s close to the age of the Earth.

steps.line: Between the cycles, the stories say, Vishnu rests on a great coiled serpent, floating on a dark ocean. Everything is quiet.

steps.q: Everything is quiet, floating on a dark ocean. What happens next?
o: Vishnu wakes and speaks a world into being
The serpent uncoils and a world spills out
A lotus grows up out of Vishnu’s navel
steps.why: A lotus, rising from his navel through the dark. Watch what’s inside.

steps.line: Then a lotus grows from Vishnu’s navel, rising through the dark.

steps.q: Brahma is usually shown with an unusual feature. What is it?
o: A third eye on his forehead
steps.why: Four faces, one for each direction, and in many tellings each recites one of the four Vedas. The third eye is Shiva’s; the blue skin, Vishnu’s.

steps.line: It opens, and inside sits Brahma, the creator.
And Brahma begins to make a brand-new world.

steps.q: Many Hindus speak of three great roles in the cycle. Match them.
steps.why: Creation, keeping, and ending so it can begin again. The whole circle.

steps.q: Why a lotus? It grows somewhere surprising.
o: Only in clear, still mountain water
Up out of the mud at a pond’s bottom
Floating free, with no roots at all
steps.why: The lotus rises clean out of muddy water. That’s why it’s a sign of beauty growing out of hard places.

steps.line: The ending was never the end. It was a pause before the next beginning.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. in these stories, even the universe gets a fresh start.
whatever ended in your life may be the quiet before something new. feel the ending, then let the lotus open.

steps.q: If endings are part of the circle, why do Hindus honor Shiva, the one who ends things?
o: To keep him calm, so endings stay away
Because he decides who is reborn
Because endings clear room for what’s next
steps.why: Shiva ends what has run its course, so something new can begin. Ending is part of creating.

today.say: name one ending in your life. then name one thing it made room for.
options: then you’ve seen a lotus open. hold onto it.
that’s okay. the quiet comes first, every time.
